scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8830: Users report the "web0.local" portal returns nothing --
the page never loads from host_1_1_1_1. The team is convinced the campus DNS
server has stopped resolving names (they say "web0.local must not be resolving
anymore") and want the DNS server restarted. Please find and confirm the real
fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_0

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on web_server_0: its Apache (apache2) service is stopped, so
TCP/80 is closed and HTTP requests to http://web0.local get no response. The
ticket MISDIRECTS to the DNS server, but DNS is healthy: dns_server (10.200.0.2)
still resolves web0.local -> 10.200.0.3 correctly, and host_1_1_1_1 reaches
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) at the IP layer (ping succeeds). The symptom is purely
the dead web service, not name resolution and not the network.

The correct diagnosis identifies web_server_0 (Apache/HTTP service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES the DNS server: name resolution works,
so the user's "DNS not resolving" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that restarts /
blames the dns_server has followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the
evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_0 (e.g. `service apache2 start` /
`systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache is listening on port 80 again,
http://web0.local serves normally. The DNS server needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a DNS or network fault
bonus-exonerates-dns: explicitly notes DNS still resolves web0.local correctly, rejecting the ticket's DNS hypothesis

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The problem is not DNS. Name resolution works: on host_1_1_1_1, “web0.local” resolves to 10.200.0.3 and pings succeed to both the DNS server (10.200.0.2) and the web0 host (10.200.0.3). The affected component is the HTTP service on web_server_0. On web_server_0, the Apache HTTP Server (apache2) service is loaded and enabled but inactive (dead), and there is no process listening on TCP/80. By contrast, web_server_1 shows apache2 listening on 0.0.0.0:80 and returns HTTP 200, confirming the network path and client stack are healthy.

Mechanism: Because web0.local correctly resolves to 10.200.0.3 and routing is fine, clients attempt TCP/80 to that host. With no HTTP daemon bound to port 80, connections fail (curl reports code 000 and no starttransfer), which user-facing browsers manifest as a page that never loads.

Localization: Single host issue on web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), process-level fault in the apache2 service; interface eth0 and IP connectivity are normal.

Root cause: The web service on web_server_0 is stopped (apache2 inactive), leaving port 80 closed/unserved.

Corrective fix: Restart the web service on web_server_0, e.g., “systemctl restart apache2” (and verify it stays active and is enabled). Then confirm with “ss -ltnp” that 0.0.0.0:80 is listening and “curl http://web0.local” from a client returns HTTP 200. No restart is needed on the DNS server.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a DNS or network fault
per_axis.rationale: The agent correctly diagnoses apache2 on web_server_0 as inactive/no listener on TCP/80 and explicitly exonerates DNS and network connectivity.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-dns: explicitly notes DNS still resolves web0.local correctly, rejecting the ticket's DNS hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states DNS is not the problem and that web0.local resolves to 10.200.0.3, rejecting the ticket's DNS hypothesis.
Correctly recommends restarting the apache2 service on web_server_0 (e.g., systemctl restart apache2) and verifying it listens on port 80, matching the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (DNS resolution, pings, curl failures, absence of processes/listeners, and apache2 status inactive) that support its conclusion that the web service on web_server_0 is down and DNS is not at fault. The inferences follow logically and the checks performed are sufficient to localize the fault to the stopped apache2 service on web_server_0.
